correctness.rationale: The published facet-label theorem is used with its full hypotheses. Centering a labeling gives the exact intrinsic normal and support value one. Central symmetry proves that a largest ball may be centered at the origin, so the inradius is the reciprocal of the largest centered-normal norm. The walk-variance lemma bounds every facet labeling by its range and endpoint visit multiplicities; its profile is strictly increasing to the maximal possible range, where the equality walk is forced. The resulting exact norm formulas give the radii and tangent counts. A Fourier-rank argument proves that odd tangent normals span the full zero-sum space, while even tangent normals span exactly the anti-periodic subspace; paired tangent inequalities then give the stated incenter uniqueness or affine dimension.

originality.rationale: Three highly relevant primary full texts were inspected: the symmetric-edge facet/cycle paper, the later facet-subgraph paper, and the weighted-cycle Kantorovich--Rubinstein paper whose unit-weight specialization is exactly the same polytope. They provide the facet structure and combinatorial identifications but no Euclidean inradius, tangent-facet, or incenter theorem. Targeted published-result and literature searches covered symmetric-edge, adjacency-polytope, KR, Lipschitz-free, cycle, inradius, insphere, and Chebyshev-center aliases. The closest existing graph-family inradius statements concern complete multipartite graphs and wheels and do not imply cycles beyond the already-covered coincidence \(C_4=K_{2,2}\).
residual_risks: An older optimal-transport source could state an equivalent Euclidean radius under Lipschitz-free or fundamental-polytope terminology not surfaced by the targeted searches.

value.rationale: Cycle symmetric edge polytopes are a basic, repeatedly studied graph family and simultaneously canonical unweighted-cycle Kantorovich--Rubinstein polytopes. The theorem gives a natural Euclidean invariant in every dimension, a closed parity-dependent formula, exact tangent-facet orbits, and a qualitative parity transition in the incenter set: unique for odd cycles but positive-dimensional for even cycles. The number of contacts remains only linear while the total facet count grows combinatorially, revealing metric structure invisible in the existing face-count and Ehrhart descriptions.
